newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS - Prices firm but volume low.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS - Prices firm but volume low.

text.p: U.S corporate bond prices firmed on the back of a stronger Treasury market on Wednesday, but trading activity remained low, traders said.
"Spreads were unchanged to tighter in most issues," said one investment-grade corporate bond trader. He added, "But volume has been low since the (Memorial Day) holiday."
Junk bond traders reported similar market conditions with prices firmer by 1/8 to 1/4 of a point on sluggish trading.
In the primary market, corporations sold over $1 billion in new investment-grade corporate bonds and capital securities.
Zurich Insurance Co sold $1 billion in 40-year capital secuities, non-callable for 10 years, via Goldman Sachs & Co.

The securities, rated AA2/AA, were priced at a spread of 133 basis points over comparable Treasuries, yielding 8.376 percent. Traders called that yield "attractive" and noted the deal was increased from an original size of $750 million to meet strong investor demand.
Banks and insurers are expected to issue a large number of these securities in the next few weeks before Congress considers whether to abolish their tax-advantaged status.
Market players said despite the looming new supply, prices in the capital securities in the secondary market have remained firm.
Elsewhere, Hilton Hotels Corp sold $300 million in five-year notes at a spread of 85 basis points over comparable Treasuries via Donaldson Lufkin & Jenrette Securities Corp.
The deal came roughly two months after Hilton sold $375 million in 10-year debt at a 110 basis point spread.
Both bonds, rated Baa1/BBB-plus, have coupon step-up features that protect investors if their rating are downgraded due to a large acquisition in the next three years.
Since January, Hilton has mounted a hostile bid to acquire ITT Corp.
Also on Wednesday, Union Tank Car sold $150 million in 12-year notes to yield 7.45 percent via Salomon Brothers Inc.
FINOVA Capital Corp, a unit of FINOVA Group Inc, sold $100 million in 10-year notes to yield 7.438 percent via Citicorp Securities Inc.

Elsewhere, bonds of wireless cable companies such as Peoples Choice TV, rose on rumors that PacTel, now a subsidiary of SBC Communications was going ahead with its plan to build a wireless cable system in California.

Wireless cable bonds, which have been trading at distressed levels for several months, dropped five to 10 points last week on speculation that PacTel would no longer go ahead with the project following its merger with SBC, market sources said.
Peoples Choice bonds rose three points to 35-37 on Wednesday, a trader said.

"This is a very speculative sector. If (today's) rumors are true, it suggests that Southwest Bell feels that there is value for this spectrum," said Oren Cohen, high-yield cable and media analyst for Bear Stearns Inc.
Calls to a PacTel spokesman were not returned.
In the broader markets, the Dow Jones industrial average dropped 26.18 points to end the day at 7357.23 on worries about the outlook for long-term interest rates.
But Treasury prices ended the day largely unchanged as a mediocre two-year note auction cancelled out gains from a positive durable goods report.
The yield on the 30-year bond closed at 7.03 percent, unchanged from Tuesday's closing level.
